**Tesla’s latest saga – a shift away from struggling models toward autonomous‑vehicle bets**  

- **Nov 6, 2026 – Cybertruck production to be wound down** – Elon Musk announced Tesla will halt production of the polarising pickup at the Austin, Texas Gigafactory in mid‑2027 to free capacity for the “Cybercab” robotaxi platform; the move follows years of weak sales, multiple recalls and recent price hikes [1][2][6][8].  
- **Oct 28 – Tesla Semi fire** – A Semi electric truck caught fire on Interstate 880, adding safety concerns to the model’s troubled rollout [14].  
- **Oct 26 – Cybertruck cancelled in Australia & New Zealand** – After seven years of deposit‑taking, Tesla scrapped plans to launch the truck in those markets, citing poor demand [15].  
- **Oct 22 – Q3 profit plunge** – Tesla reported a 43 % drop in third‑quarter earnings, blamed on lower vehicle deliveries and higher warranty/recall costs [16].  
- **Oct 18 – Roadster reservation uncertainty** – The company warned it “cannot guarantee” that reservation holders will ever receive the promised next‑generation Roadster, fueling doubts about the project’s viability [17].  
- **Oct 14 – NHTSA robotaxi petition** – Regulators received a petition alleging Tesla’s autonomous‑driving system may be unsafe in school zones, highlighting growing scrutiny of the robotaxi push [20].  

*Overall picture*: Tesla is scaling back under‑performing hardware (Cybertruck, Semi, Roadster) while reallocating resources to its autonomous‑vehicle strategy (Cybercab/robotaxis), even as it faces profit pressure and regulatory challenges. All points are drawn directly from the listed news items.
